findings.text: follow-on: the per-mutation negative-control logs name the node's base revision for a head-derived tree. Both m1 (line 1: 'revision: ea69eb30... (scratch tree, mutation 1 only)') and m2 name ea69eb30, yet each scratch conftest.py is the head tree (d242c8ae) with one targeted revert, and the combined negative-control.log names the head 455a7266. A reader reconstructing a tree from the m1/m2 header would materialise the pre-fix conftest rather than the mutated head, so the header does not name the revision the run measured — the same class of mislabel as defect (3) this node repaired.

follow-on: _holder_is_live returns True (live, so refused) whenever the lock record carries no 'start' value, so a lock written before this change whose pid an unrelated process later reuses is still refused indefinitely; the exactness holds only for locks the new code writes, and no case covers the legacy-lock path. Bounded and self-healing (such locks exist only until the next acquisition rewrites them) but unstated in the evidence fragment.

justifications.durability: each new case fails under its own declared mutation and passes at head, and the live-holder, dead-pid and sequential paths remain covered (case1 asserts the refusal names the holder's pid and the basetemp and the first session's pid-named fixture survives; case3 drives a dead pid). Caveats: the partial-write mutation reddens case5 through FileNotFoundError in the test's own mtime-refresh loop (the mutated session unlinks the held lock) rather than through the case's refusal assertion at line 324 — the id does fail, so the control holds, but the assertion the case was written for is not the one that fires; and no case covers a legacy lock that carries no start time.
justifications.evidence: the head gate, the combined negative control and both per-mutation controls are logged with revision, tree and literal command, and this reviewer independently re-ran all four arms (head 5 passed/EXIT=0; m1 1 failed/EXIT=1; m2 2 failed/EXIT=1; combined 2 failed/EXIT=1), but the m1 and m2 logs name the base revision ea69eb30 while their trees are the head with one revert, so those two header lines do not name the revision they measured.
justifications.fit: the helpers follow conftest's module-level idiom, the docstrings state the mechanism (a pid is not an identity because the kernel reuses pids; the lock is linked into place so it never exists unread), comments explain why rather than what, and no plan label, ticket, version name or author attribution is introduced.
justifications.goal_fidelity: tests/conftest.py:423-449 reads field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat, :467-486 treats a live pid whose recorded start time differs as stale, :498-519 writes the holder to a temporary sibling and os.link's it into place, and :543-544 refuses an empty or unparseable lock younger than five seconds; the reused-pid and partial-write cases at tests/test_a_shared_basetemp_is_refused.py:271-326 exercise the first two, and the fragment's head arm now names 2225ab398 — exactly the done-when.
justifications.scope_discipline: only tests/conftest.py, the test file and the two evidence fragments change, all inside the manifest's declared write paths, with no product source touched and no test skipped, xfailed, deleted or weakened.
